name: ME-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Chellie Pingree seeks re-election with a large cash advantage
Republican Ronald Russell has raised little and has no outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Pingree: an 11-point Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of roughly $400,000 with no outside spending against her. Markets price her near certain, and no polls or ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing Russell within single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Chellie Pingree is seeking another term in a southern Maine district that voted about 11 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. She holds a decisive financial edge, with roughly $423,000 on hand compared with about $20,000 for Republican Ronald Russell, and no outside groups are spending in the race. Prediction markets put her chances near 96 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Those fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit win, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any specific sign of a competitive race.
